42: /** Every library write is a read-modify-write of the *entire* 16-key blob, so without a
43:  *  precondition two admins editing unrelated records in unrelated collections silently clobber
44:  *  each other — last writer wins, and the changelog records both as successful. `version` is the
45:  *  row's `updated_at` exactly as Postgres returned it; hand it back to `saveLibrary` to make the
46:  *  write conditional.
47:  *
48:  *  Caveat worth knowing: this is millisecond-resolution time, not a monotonic counter, so two
49:  *  writes landing inside the same millisecond could both pass the check. Closing that properly
50:  *  needs a real version column and a migration; for a tool with a handful of admins the time
51:  *  precondition removes the realistic window, and it needs no schema change. */
52: export async function getLibraryWithVersion(): Promise<{ library: Library; version: string }> {
53:   const { data, error } = await supabaseAdmin.from('library').select('data, updated_at').eq('id', 'singleton').maybeSingle();
54:   if (error) throw error;
55:   if (!data) throw new Error('Library not seeded');
56:   const raw = data.data as Library;
57:   const version = data.updated_at as string;
58:   const normalized = normalizeLibrary(raw);
59:   // Self-heal a Library row missing a field added after it was seeded, so future reads don't
60:   // need to repeat this — same pattern as getSheet's Recoveries/Scars backfill. Compares every
61:   // key rather than the six this used to name by hand: villains/npcs/locations (0.35.0) and
62:   // loadTiers were all added later and were never in that list, so a row missing one of them
63:   // re-normalized on every single read and never healed.
64:   const healed = (Object.keys(normalized) as (keyof Library)[]).some((k) => normalized[k] !== raw[k]);
65:   if (healed) {
66:     try {
67:       return { library: normalized, version: await saveLibrary(normalized, version) };
68:     } catch (err) {
69:       // Another request healed it first. Ours is equivalent, so serve it and let the caller's
70:       // own write fail its precondition if it has one — never fail a *read* over this.
71:       if (!(err instanceof LibraryConflictError)) throw err;
72:     }
73:   }
74:   return { library: normalized, version };
75: }

77: export async function getLibrary(): Promise<Library> {
78:   return (await getLibraryWithVersion()).library;
79: }

81: /** Returns the new version (the row's `updated_at` as Postgres stored it), so a caller doing
82:  *  several writes in a row can chain preconditions. Omitting `expectedVersion` writes
83:  *  unconditionally — that's the seed/import/reset path, where replacing whatever is there is the
84:  *  whole point; per-record edits should always pass one. */
85: export async function saveLibrary(lib: Library, expectedVersion?: string): Promise<string> {
86:   if (expectedVersion === undefined) {
87:     const { data, error } = await supabaseAdmin
88:       .from('library')
89:       .upsert({ id: 'singleton', data: lib, updated_at: nowIso() })
90:       .select('updated_at')
91:       .maybeSingle();
92:     if (error) throw error;
93:     return (data?.updated_at as string) ?? nowIso();
94:   }
95: 
96:   const { data, error } = await supabaseAdmin
97:     .from('library')
98:     .update({ data: lib, updated_at: nowIso() })
99:     .eq('id', 'singleton')
100:     .eq('updated_at', expectedVersion)
101:     .select('updated_at');
102:   if (error) throw error;
103:   if (!data || data.length === 0) throw new LibraryConflictError();
104:   return data[0].updated_at as string;
105: }

89:  *  Mutates `sheet` in place. When it reports `Crumbled: true` nothing was marked, and the caller
90:  *  owns the rest of the consequence: choosing which Condition to clear (V0.5 leaves that to the
91:  *  player) and narrating leaving the scene. Combat used to also grant a flat Vulnerable-4 Status
92:  *  here (`applyCrumbleVulnerable` in `combat.ts`) — V0.6 slice 1 deletes that clause from Crumble
93:  *  entirely, so the only remaining consequence is the movement restriction, which is a table rule
94:  *  this app doesn't enforce. */
95: export function markCondition(sheet: CharacterSheet, virtueId: string): { Crumbled: boolean } {
96:   // Order matters, and it is not obvious. The all-marked check has to come FIRST: when every
97:   // Condition is marked there is nowhere to put this one no matter which Virtue was named, so it
98:   // Crumbles — including when the named Virtue happens to be one of the already-marked ones.
99:   // Checking "already marked" first would swallow exactly that case and silently do nothing,
100:   // which is what this did before its own test caught it.
101:   if (allConditionsMarked(sheet)) return { Crumbled: true };
102:   const vv = sheet.Virtues.find((v) => v.VirtueId === virtueId);
103:   // Below five, re-marking a marked Virtue is a plain no-op, not a Crumble — the player could
104:   // have picked a different one, so nothing is forced.
105:   if (vv?.ConditionMarked) return { Crumbled: false };
106:   if (vv) vv.ConditionMarked = true;
107:   return { Crumbled: false };
108: }

241: /** Applies the completion choices to a holder whose Quest is complete (three Act Breaks). Throws if
242:  *  the Quest isn't complete. Returns whether the caller should fill the progress track to its cap
243:  *  and advance immediately. Mutates `holder` in place. */
244: export function completeQuest(holder: QuestHolder, choices: QuestCompletionChoices): { fillProgress: boolean } {
245:   if (holder.ActBreaks < 3) {
246:     throw new Error('This Quest is not complete yet.');
247:   }
248:   if (choices.NewName !== undefined) {
249:     const trimmed = choices.NewName.trim();
250:     if (trimmed) holder.Name = trimmed;
251:   }
252:   if (choices.SkillTags !== undefined) {
253:     holder.SkillTags = choices.SkillTags.map((t) => t.trim()).filter(Boolean);
254:   }
255:   if (choices.FlawTags !== undefined) {
256:     holder.FlawTags = choices.FlawTags.map((t) => t.trim()).filter(Boolean);
257:   }
258:   if (choices.NewQuest !== undefined) {
259:     const trimmed = choices.NewQuest.trim();
260:     if (trimmed) {
261:       holder.Quest = trimmed;
262:       holder.ActBreaks = 0;
263:       holder.Forsakes = 0;
264:     }
265:   }
266:   return { fillProgress: choices.FillProgress === true };
267: }

269: /** Applies the abandonment procedure to a holder whose Quest has three Forsakes. Throws if it
270:  *  hasn't. Returns how much progress (Potential or Rapport) the caller must add — "Add Potential
271:  *  equal to the total number of Forsakes and Act Breaks to the new Motif, taking a Motif Advance if
272:  *  you mark 5 Potential". Mutates `holder` in place. */
273: export function abandonQuest(holder: QuestHolder, input: QuestAbandonInput): { progressToAdd: number } {
274:   if (holder.Forsakes < 3) {
275:     throw new Error('This Quest has not been abandoned.');
276:   }
277:   const skillTrimmed = input.SkillTag.trim();
278:   const flawTrimmed = input.FlawTag.trim();
279:   const questTrimmed = input.NewQuest.trim();
280:   const nameTrimmed = input.NewName.trim();
281:   if (!skillTrimmed || !flawTrimmed || !questTrimmed || !nameTrimmed) {
282:     throw new Error('Abandoning a Quest needs a new name, one Skill Tag, one Flaw Tag and a new Quest.');
283:   }
284:   const progressToAdd = holder.ActBreaks + holder.Forsakes;
285:   holder.Name = nameTrimmed;
286:   holder.SkillTags = [skillTrimmed];
287:   holder.FlawTags = [flawTrimmed];
288:   holder.Quest = questTrimmed;
289:   holder.ActBreaks = 0;
290:   holder.Forsakes = 0;
291:   return { progressToAdd };
292: }

296: /** "Choose two Hero Improvements. You can only get a Starting Improvement on any Improvement Tree
297:  *  first. Then, for your second Improvement, you may choose a second Starting Improvement or an
298:  *  Improvement connected by a line to another Improvement you already have on that same tree. Each
299:  *  can only be chosen once." (Ruleset-V0.6.md, "Choose Hero Improvements"). Returns `null` when
300:  *  `ids` is a legal starting pair, otherwise a player-facing reason. Order-insensitive: the pair is
301:  *  legal if at least one is a Starting Improvement and the other is either Starting too or is
302:  *  unlocked by it (`improvementState`). */
303: export function validateStartingImprovements(ids: readonly string[], improvements: readonly Improvement[]): string | null {
304:   if (ids.length !== 2) return 'Choose exactly two Hero Improvements.';
305:   if (ids[0] === ids[1]) return 'Each Hero Improvement can only be chosen once.';
306:   const imp0 = improvements.find((i) => i.Id === ids[0]);
307:   const imp1 = improvements.find((i) => i.Id === ids[1]);
308:   if (!imp0 || !imp1) return 'One or more Hero Improvements are not recognized.';
309: 
310:   // Try each arrangement: one as "first", one as "second"
311:   // First arrangement: imp0 first, imp1 second
312:   if (imp0.IsStarting) {
313:     const state = improvementState(imp1, new Set([ids[0]]));
314:     if (state === 'available') return null;
315:   }
316:   // Second arrangement: imp1 first, imp0 second
317:   if (imp1.IsStarting) {
318:     const state = improvementState(imp0, new Set([ids[1]]));
319:     if (state === 'available') return null;
320:   }
321: 
322:   return 'This is not a legal starting pair.';
323: }

361:  *  Skill/Weakness Tag options above — the party-level analog of `takeMotifAdvance`. `tag` is the
362:  *  new tag's text for `AddSkillTag`/`AddWeaknessTag`; `RemoveWeaknessTag` pops the most recently

365:  *  `cap` (`GameSettings.RapportTrackLength`) is subtracted, not reset to 0 — V0.6 slice 7's own
366:  *  Rapport-overflow rule (`WorkPlan-V0.6.md` Section A4 item 1): a banked overflow beyond the cap

369:  *  advance just needs the player to tap it again — no loop needed here). Mutates `party` in
370:  *  place. */

372:   party.Rapport = Math.max(0, party.Rapport - cap);

380:     party.WeaknessTags.push(trimmed);
381:     effect = `Weakness Tag: ${trimmed}`;
382:   } else if (option === 'RemoveWeaknessTag') {
383:     const removed = party.WeaknessTags.pop();
384:     effect = removed ? `Removed Weakness Tag: ${removed}` : 'No Weakness Tag to remove.';
385:   }
386:   party.History.unshift({ Id: newId('h'), At: nowIso(), Action: 'took', Name: 'Progress the Party', Effect: effect });

455:  *  function below hardcoded a literal 5 until 0.50.0, so raising the setting rendered more pips
456:  *  (`AdvancementPanel` reads `count={bondLen}`) than the logic would ever fill. One number governs

459:  *  rather than in the code. The default keeps every existing call site behaving identically. */

462: /** V0.5: "When you place your 5th Bond at Bond 5, your Bond Level locks and can not be moved
463:  *  down. You can no longer spend Bond on that track." A maxed Bond (Level and Bond Track both at
464:  *  `cap`) is locked — no stored field needed, it's fully derived from the two numbers already on
465:  *  `Bond`. This rule is unchanged from the pre-V0.5 ruleset; only its vocabulary moved from Kin
466:  *  to Bond. */
467: export function isBondLocked(bond: Bond, cap = DEFAULT_BOND_CAP): boolean {
468:   return bond.BondLevel >= cap && bond.BondTrack >= cap;

471: /** Spending Bond is unilateral — either partner may do it without the other's approval (the
472:  * game's rules text says "either PC on the Bond Track can spend Bond", unlike Forging, which
473:  * needs both to agree), so it applies immediately rather than going through the propose/accept
474:  * handshake. Mutates `bond` in place; returns a short detail string for the log. Throws
475:  * `BondHandshakeError` if the Bond is locked (see `isBondLocked`) rather than silently dropping
476:  * it back below Level 5. */
477: export function applySpendBond(bond: Bond, delta = 1, cap = DEFAULT_BOND_CAP): string {
478:   if (isBondLocked(bond, cap)) {
479:     throw new BondHandshakeError(`This Bond is locked at Level ${cap} with a full Bond Track — Bond can no longer be spent on it.`);
480:   }
481:   bond.BondTrack = bond.BondTrack - delta;
482:   if (bond.BondTrack < 0) {
483:     bond.BondLevel = Math.max(0, bond.BondLevel - 1);
484:     bond.BondTrack = cap - 1;
485:   }
486:   return 'Bond now ' + bond.BondTrack;
487: }

489: /** Mutates `bond` in place per the accepted proposal's type. Returns a short detail string for the log. */
490: export function resolveAcceptedBond(bond: Bond, cap = DEFAULT_BOND_CAP): string {
491:   const p = bond.PendingChange;
492:   if (!p) return '';
493:   let detail = '';
494:   if (p.Type === 'MarkBond') {
495:     bond.BondTrack = Math.min(cap, bond.BondTrack + (p.Payload.Delta || 1));
496:     detail = 'Bond now ' + bond.BondTrack;
497:   } else if (p.Type === 'SpendBond') {
498:     // No longer reachable via the normal UI (SpendBond applies immediately — see
499:     // applySpendBond above) — kept so a proposal created before that change can still resolve.
500:     detail = applySpendBond(bond, p.Payload.Delta || 1, cap);
501:   } else if (p.Type === 'ForgeBond') {
502:     bond.BondLevel = Math.min(cap, bond.BondLevel + 1);
503:     bond.BondTrack = 0;
504:     bond.BondMoves = (bond.BondMoves || []).concat([{ Level: bond.BondLevel, Text: p.Payload.Text || '', AuthoredAt: nowIso() }]);
505:     detail = 'Bond Level ' + bond.BondLevel;
506:   }
507:   bond.PendingChange = null;
508:   bond.UpdatedAt = nowIso();
509:   return detail;
510: }
